title: Senior's toolkit: dates and time series
summary: Parsing timestamps safely, resample with current aliases, rolling windows, growth, and time zones that match the business.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: dates and time series
steps.body: Time data breaks in quiet ways: a day boundary in the wrong time zone, a 7-row window that is not 7 days, a month alias that changed. These are the calls and arguments that keep daily and monthly numbers right.

toolkit.what: Parse timestamps once, at load time, with the format stated. Guessing formats can swap day and month.
flags: say the format; parsing is also much faster
convert everything to UTC (mixed offsets become one zone)
bad values become NaT instead of raising

toolkit.what: Group a datetime index into regular periods. pandas 2.2 renamed the period-end aliases (`"ME"`, `"QE"`, `"YE"`, lowercase `"h"`) and warned on the old ones; pandas 3 rejects the old ones with a `ValueError`.
flags: day / week (weeks end on Sunday by default)
month end / month start (the old `"M"` is an error in pandas 3)
hour / minute (the old `"H"` and `"T"` are errors in pandas 3)

toolkit.what: Moving windows such as a 7-day average. A number counts rows; a string such as `"7D"` counts time, which is correct when days are missing.
flags: the last 7 days, on a datetime index
give a result even before the window is full
label the window by its middle

toolkit.what: Compare each period with an earlier one: yesterday's value, the change, the growth rate.
`tz_localize` says which zone naive timestamps are in; `tz_convert` changes an aware timestamp to another zone. Store UTC, report in the business's zone.
flags: attach a zone to naive times
show aware times in another zone
what to do with the clock-change hour

toolkit.what: Date parts of a datetime column, without a loop.
Make the missing dates visible. A day with no sales is a row with 0, not a missing row, or windows and charts lie.
flags: one row per day, NaN where data was missing

steps.prompt: The New York store manager says Monday's sales in your report include Sunday evening orders. Timestamps are stored in UTC. What is the fix?
options: Convert to the store's zone before grouping: `df["ts"].dt.tz_convert("America/New_York")`, then resample by day
steps.explain: Days are cut at midnight in the index's zone. In UTC, 8 pm Sunday in New York is already Monday. A fixed offset is wrong for half the year because of daylight saving; the named zone handles it.

steps.prompt: `daily.rolling(7).mean()` gives a "7-day average", but the shop was closed on several days and those dates have no rows. What is wrong?
options: `7` means 7 rows, which can span more than 7 days; use `rolling("7D")`, or add the missing days first with `asfreq("D", fill_value=0)`
Use `resample("7D")` instead of rolling, which is the same thing
steps.explain: A row-based window ignores the calendar. A time-based window or a complete daily index fixes it. `resample("7D")` makes non-overlapping blocks, which is a different question.

steps.prompt: An old notebook that ran on pandas 2 now fails on pandas 3 at `resample("M")` with `ValueError: Invalid frequency: M. Failed to parse with error message: ValueError("'M' is no longer supported for offsets. Please use 'ME' instead.")`. What do you change?
options: `resample("ME")`, the month-end alias (or `"MS"` for month start)
Pin pandas below 3 so the old alias keeps working
steps.explain: pandas 2.2 split aliases into period ends (`ME`, `QE`, `YE`) and starts (`MS`, `QS`, `YS`), with a FutureWarning on the old names; pandas 3 removed them. `"30D"` is not a calendar month, lowercase `"m"` is rejected too, and pinning an old pandas only postpones the one-line fix.

steps.prompt: Match each alias or argument to its meaning.
pairs: a window of seven days of time
a result before the window is full

steps.prompt: Parse ISO timestamps with mixed offsets into UTC, then total the amount per day.
steps.explain: `utc=True` turns every offset into one UTC column. `resample` groups a datetime index into periods; `rolling` would make overlapping windows.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Parse dates once with an explicit `format`, store them in UTC and convert to the business's time zone only to report. Fill missing days before rolling or charting, and when someone says a daily number is off by a little, check the time zone first.
